ops.title: TestRegisterTranscript is load-sensitive: fixed 30s registerTimeout around a /bin/sh shim
ops.description:
register.go:24 `const registerTimeout = 30 * time.Second` bounds an
exec.CommandContext (register.go:132-142) around the capt-hook registration
call. TestRegisterTranscript plants a `#!/bin/sh` shim and asserts on its exit
code, so the test inherits that fixed 30s budget for a subprocess spawn.

On a host whose execs are serialized (see below) that budget is not enough, and
the context kills the shim before it runs:

    --- FAIL: TestRegisterTranscript (81.80s)
        --- FAIL: TestRegisterTranscript/failed_shim_nonzero (30.01s)
            register_test.go:151: outcome = "failed rc=-1: signal: killed", want "failed rc=3: boom"
        --- FAIL: TestRegisterTranscript/uvx_fallback (30.01s)
            register_test.go:164: outcome = "failed rc=-1: signal: killed", want "ok 019f-abc"

Evidence that this is load sensitivity and not a logic error:

  - `signal: killed` at exactly 30.01s and 30.02s — the registerTimeout bound
    itself, not a wrong value.
  - Non-deterministic: on re-run, uvx_fallback passed and only
    failed_shim_nonzero failed. A logic error fails both, every time.
  - The same commit returned `ok 76.459s` at load average 3.2, and failed at
    load 33.79 (1049.085s) and again at 33.79 on a targeted -run.
  - The thing being spawned is `/bin/sh`, which on macOS hosts running
    EndpointSecurity agents (SentinelOne + Kandji here) costs ~687ms per exec
    and is serialized machine-wide at roughly 4 execs/sec. Measured on this
    host: /bin/sh 687ms, /usr/bin/env 537ms, /bin/bash 259ms, a Go binary 6.5ms;
    24 concurrent execs of a system binary take 6.2s wall, i.e. no parallelism.

Green on a quiet CI runner (macos-latest), red on a loaded developer box, so it
surfaces as an unreproducible flake rather than a hard failure.

Fix direction: either bound the shim spawn independently of the production
registerTimeout — the test does not need the production bound to assert an exit
code — or make the timeout configurable/load-aware rather than a fixed 30s, so
the same constant does not serve both an orphaned worker's real deadline and a
unit test's subprocess.

ops.text: TestRegisterTranscript passes on a developer machine at load average 30+
The shim spawn is bounded independently of, or proportionally to, the test's own deadline
The 30s bound still protects the orphaned worker path it was written for
